Definition: properly, an adult (as of full length); by implication, a man (only in the plural)
BiblicalUsage: The word means men, and it is almost always used of fewness: the LORD will scatter Israel so that only a few men are left, and the psalm remembers when they were but a few in number. Jacob says the same of his household when he fears the Canaanites: we are few in number, and they will gather against us.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word keeps showing up where God's people are small and outnumbered, and that is the point: God has always done His greatest work with a few.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
